title: Pull the plug (naive in-place writer)

events.label: setup: report.txt = A
events.detail: The naive way: one file, A (64 x 0x41), fully durable. Now save B over it in place.

events.label: naive save: open(O_TRUNC) + write B  [crash at after_trunc]
events.detail: What most code does: truncate the file and write the new bytes over the only copy.

events.label: open report.txt O_TRUNC
events.detail: The naive writer opens the ONLY copy of the document with O_TRUNC: the old content is thrown away before a single new byte exists.

events.label: CRASH at after_trunc (kill -9)
events.detail: The process dies in the middle of overwriting the only copy. There is no old version to go back to.

events.label: reopen: read report.txt (no recovery possible)
events.detail: The naive format has no journal, no checksum, no second copy: whatever bytes are in the file ARE the document.

events.label: read() = empty (0 B)
events.detail: The truncate reached the file, the new data never did: the document is GONE.

events.label: naive in-place save is NOT crash-safe: document is neither A nor B (expected)

checks.name: naive in-place save is NOT crash-safe: document is neither A nor B (expected)

summary: Naive writer crashed at after_trunc: the document is EMPTY.
